44734add.reply: The record must preserve Russia's proposal to replace paragraph 6's explicit humanitarian list with a reference to GA resolution 46/182. It must also note Russia's withdrawal of draft S/2020/25 after Resolution 2504 was adopted. No named actors, decisions, reasons, or qualifications are supplied in the source.
required: Russia's oral amendment proposed a change to paragraph 6 of S/2020/24
replace the explicit humanitarian principles with a reference to General Assembly resolution 46/182
Russia withdrew separate draft S/2020/25 in light of adoption of Resolution 2504
44734add.source: Russia proposed an oral amendment to paragraph 6 of S/2020/24. It would replace the explicit list of humanitarian principles with a reference to the guiding principles in General Assembly resolution 46/182. After Resolution 2504 was adopted, Russia withdrew its separate draft S/2020/25 in light of that adoption.

9ce80ce7.reply: Belgium, speaking for Germany, argued Russia's amendment conflicted with the cross-border mechanism. They requested the Council adopt the penholders' text, noting no viable alternative existed to Al-Yarubiyah. The draft asked the Secretary-General to examine alternatives by February's end.
required: Belgium speaking for itself and Germany argued the Russian amendment conflicted with the exceptional cross-border mechanism
called for adoption of their original draft
no viable current alternative to Al-Yarubiyah and a request for the Secretary-General to examine alternatives by the end of February
9ce80ce7.source: Belgium, also speaking for Germany, argued that Russia's oral amendment conflicted with the exceptional cross-border mechanism and asked the Council to adopt the penholders' text as presented. It said there was no viable alternative then to Al-Yarubiyah and that the draft asked the Secretary-General to examine alternatives by the end of February.

cc4f9bab.reply: The Council voted on Russia's oral amendment to the Belgium–Germany draft, receiving three votes for, seven against, and five abstentions, causing it to fail. Subsequently, the Council voted on S/2020/24. No named actors, specific decisions, reasons, or qualifications were supplied in the source.
required: Russian oral amendment to the Belgium–Germany draft voted on before S/2020/24
three in favour, seven against and five abstentions
failed because it lacked the required number of votes
cc4f9bab.source: The Council put Russia's oral amendment to the Belgium–Germany draft to a vote first under the procedure for textual additions or deletions. It received three votes in favour, seven against and five abstentions and failed to obtain the required number of votes. The Council then voted on S/2020/24.
